content.GLOSS: To perceive with the eyes; to discern, understand, or witness.
content.ART_PROMPT: A luminous eye-like opening formed by dark storm clouds, a single iris at its center, with restrained golden rays falling onto a narrow reflective river; symbolic biblical illustration, no human face, no portrait, and no people.
content.ABILITY_TEXT: Look at the top 3 cards of the Tower, then return them in any order.
content.OT_VERSE_LINE: Psalm 34:8 — “Taste and see that the LORD is good; blessed is the one who takes refuge in him.”
content.NT_VERSE_LINE: Matthew 5:8 — “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.”
TRIVIA_BULLETS: The Hebrew verb 'ra'ah' is the root of 'ro'eh' (seer), an early title for prophets.
Hagar names God 'El Roi' (The God Who Sees Me) in Genesis 16, the only occurrence of this title.
In the Bible, physical sight is often a metaphor for spiritual understanding or faith.
The Greek 'horaō' implies not just catching sight of something, but mentally discerning it.
